name: Sanballat
overview: Sanballat the Horonite is depicted in Scripture as a persistent adversary of the Jewish people during the critical period of rebuilding Jerusalem after the Babylonian captivity. He, along with others like Tobiah and Geshem, opposed the restoration efforts, reacting with grief and mockery at the work to seek Israel's welfare. Additionally, Sanballat's influence extended through familial ties, as seen when a son of the high priest was connected to him by marriage, prompting Nehemiah to take decisive action to preserve the community's integrity.
